The witness records a pe after MT 11:13 (single witness), at the seam this unit opens on at 11:14. Close: oshb:Ezek.11.21 וְאֶל לֵ֧ב שִׁקּוּצֵיהֶ֛ם וְתוֹעֲבוֹתֵיהֶ֖ם לִבָּ֣ם הֹלֵ֑ךְ דַּרְכָּם֙ בְּרֹאשָׁ֣ם נָתַ֔תִּי נְאֻ֖ם אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהוִֽה ends with the utterance formula נאם אדני יהוה (one of the book's 81 utterance-close verses). Both sides are formula-clean: a strict word-event onset and an utterance close, the tightest formula bracket in this span. This is the embedded salvation oracle the assignment specifically raises: it stands inside the still-open vision (the courtyard scene has not yet returned the prophet — that happens only at 11:22-25) but is bounded by its own onset and close formulae independent of the vision frame, so it is set as its own row rather than folded into 11:1-13 or 11:22-25.

literature_type_guess: the Noah-Daniel-Job oracle: even these three could save only their own souls, applied to Jerusalem
device_notes: MT 14:14 and MT 14:20 both carry the Qere-adaptation editorial note class disclosed above, in addition to the ordinary ketiv/qere note at each verse (ketiv דנאל, qere דָּנִיֵּ֣אל (oshb:Ezek.14.14 and oshb:Ezek.14.20) — the shorter legendary-figure spelling against the fuller ‘Daniel’ reading); both disclosures are given at both verses since they are two independent single-witness apparatus facts about the same word. Paseq at 14:21 is count-only. oshb:Ezek.15.1 is cited above only as forward-side onset evidence for the seam; it is not a row here.
